citations.claim: EW approach E waits 200 s at red with queue 91 while NS holds green just before violation
first max_wait violation: E waits 201 s at red with queue 91 while NS still green

counterfactual.change: Removed the single detector_fail event on N (t=562, duration 164); same 686 steps, all else identical. Predicted to remove failure because NS green can then terminate normally; it ran with zero violations.

explanation: NS green starts ~step 489-490 and is still held at step 686 (~197 s), far beyond max_green_seconds=87, while EW approaches E/W wait at red with large queues (75+ s by step 560, 91/200 at step 685, 91/201 at 686). The N detector_fail active from t=562 covers the period when max-green expiry/recall should have ended NS green (~step 576). The controller therefore fails to enforce max-green / long-wait recall while a detector on the green direction has failed, starving EW past the 200 s max_wait limit. Removing the detector_fail event eliminates the violation.

violation.detail: approach 1 has waited 201 s at red with vehicles queued (limit 200)

vision_note: Long blue queues on the east and south approaches remain stopped at red signals across steps 683 to 686 with no movement. The north-south approaches appear to hold green throughout, so the queued directions are starved indefinitely.
